content.title: Real Madrid vs. Man City head to head history, all UEFA Champions League matches over the years | Sporting News
content.text: Real Madrid and Manchester City cannot stay away from one another in the UEFA Champions League.The December 2025 league-phase meeting between the teams was already the sixth time in the past seven seasons they had faced off in the competition. Editor's Picks City were the winners on that occasion but when they reconvened for the Round of 16, Madrid regained the upper hand with a 5-1 aggregate victory, a triumph underpinned by Federico Valverde's brilliant first-leg hat-trick.This modern European rivalry shows drama is more or less guaranteed when they come together. The Sporting News looks back at the history of this matchup.MORE: Champions League knockout phase draw result, bracket for Round of 16 and beyond in 2026Real Madrid vs. Man City history, previous meetingsThe sides first met amid the relatively low-stakes of the 2012/13 group stage before a semifinal showdown in 2016.There was a knockout tie in 2020, with the two legs separated by an unprecedented six months due to the coronavirus lockdown, before an unforgettable semifinal epic in 2022.DateHome teamAway teamResult03/17/2026Man CityReal Madrid1-203/11/2026Real MadridMan City3-012/10/2025Real MadridMan City1-202/19/2025Real MadridMan City3-102/11/2025Man CityReal Madrid2-304/17/2024Man CityReal Madrid1-1 (3-4 pens)04/09/2024Real MadridMan City3-305/17/2023Man CityReal Madrid4-005/09/2023Real MadridMan City1-105/04/2022Real MadridMan City3-104/26/2022Man CityReal Madrid4-308/07/2020Man CityReal Madrid2-102/26/2020Real MadridMan City1-205/04/2016Real MadridMan City1-004/26/2016Man CityReal Madrid0-011/21/2012Man CityReal Madrid1-109/18/2012Real MadridMan City3-2Real Madrid vs. Man City head-to-headIn total, these teams have met 10th 7 times in this competition. Real Madrid have won seven games, Manchester City have won five games, and five have ended in draws.City won their first Champions League title in 2023 under Pep Guardiola. Madrid have won the tournament a record 15 times in their history.Below are some of the most memorable meetings between these sides.MORE: Teams with the most UEFA Champions League titlesReal Madrid vs. Man City (2012 Group Stage)The clubs played out a thriller in the Santiago Bernabeu, with goalkeeper Joe Hart keeping City in the game before Edin Dzeko gave them the lead with an hour played after a surging Yaya Toure breakaway.Marcelo levelled with a deflected strike, only for Aleksandar Kolarov to curl home a free kick from the right.But, in a sting in the tale to foreshadow what would unfold between the teams almost a decade later, Karim Benzema equalised before Cristiano Ronaldo fired a last-gasp winner to snatch a 3-2 triumph. Madrid boss Jose Mourinho ripped his suit doing a knee-slide celebration on the pitch.In the return game, City were eliminated from the group stage for the second season in succession. Benzema put Madrid ahead before City, needing a win to maintain their chances of progressing, levelled through a Sergio Aguero penalty and it finished 1-1.Real Madrid vs. Man City (2016 Semifinals)City received a boost ahead of their first Champions League semifinal when Cristiano Ronaldo was ruled out of the first leg in Manchester.That was the first of two turgid games that were settled by City midfielder Fernando putting through his own goal in the Bernabeu — the only goal in either leg.Madrid went on to win the first of three Champions Leagues in a row under Zinedine Zidane when they defeated Atletico Madrid on penalties in Milan.Real Madrid vs. Man City (2020 Round of 16)City performed masterfully in a striker-less formation in Madrid, only to fall behind against the run of play when Isco broke the deadlock during the second half.Guardiola sent on Raheem Sterling from the bench and reverted to a more conventional setup, with Kevin De Bruyne crossing for Gabriel Jesus to equalise. Sterling was then brought down by Dani Carvajal for De Bruyne to seal a 2-1 first-leg advantage from the penalty spot.That game was in February 2020 and unprecedented circumstances meant the Manchester leg taking place behind closed doors in August. Sterling gave City an early lead and Jesus made sure of progression to the truncated finals tournament in Lisbon — where City collapsed in a heap against Lyon —- after Benzema equalised on the night.Real Madrid vs. Man City (2022 Semifinals)Benzema honestly seems to relish games between these two teams and he almost single-handedly kept Madrid in this tie after De Bruyne and Jesus opened up an early 2-0 lead in Manchester.Riyad Mahrez missed a glorious chance for a third and Benzema reduced the arrears before halftime. Afterwards, goals from Phil Foden and Bernardo Silva were split by a sensational solo goal from Vinicius Junior. Aymeric Laporte’s late handball and a nerve-less Panenka penalty from Benzema ensured City only took a 4-3 advantage to Madrid.A cagey clash at the Bernabeu looked to have been settled when Mahrez crowned an excellent City break late in the second half. But Madrid’s taste for logic-defying Champions League comebacks again came to the fore as a brace from substitute Rodrygo forced extra time.A more conventional Benzema spot kick in the additional period was enough to break City hearts.Real Madrid vs. Man City (2023 Semifinals)City headed into the encounter at the Bernabeu with a different beast in their corner: Erling Haaland.Yet the Norwegian, who already had 51 goals to his name for the season, was unusually quiet by his standards as Antonio Rudiger kept him quiet. City dominated the early exchanges but it was Real who took the lead on 36 minutes with a stunning strike from Vinicius Jr. on the edge of the box.The second leg was a different story. Bernardo Silva gave City a deserved lead, and they proceeded to dominate every step of the way to a 4-0 victory, Manuel Akanji and Julian Alvarez netting in the second half after Silva had scored his second.Real Madrid vs. Man City (2024 Quarterfinals)Andriy Lunin should have done better with both his wall alignment and the attempt to keep Bernardo Silva's second-minute free-kick out of his net but a Ruben Dias own goal and a Rodrygo solo effort had Madrid 2-1 to the good inside 15 minutes.City stepped things up after halftime and Phil Foden pulled them level with his 22nd goal of the season before Josko Gvardiol dispatched a similarly impressive long-ranger for his first goal for the club. Vinicius Junior's chipped cross was emphatically volleyed home by Federico Valverde to leave everything up for grabs.In the second leg, Madrid looked to be set to hold on to a 1-0 lead through Rodrygo, but Kevin De Bruyne finally broke their resistance with a close-range finish after Antonio Rudiger failed to clear the ball.Guardiola took off his goalscorer and Erling Haaland for extra time, in which not a great deal happened. Luka Modric missed Madrid's first penalty, but Lunin saved from Silva and Mateo Kovacic, allowing Rudiger to atone for his earlier error by converting the decisive spot-kick.Real Madrid vs. Man City (2025 Knockout playoffs)Poor campaigns in the inaugural league phase meant a much earlier meeting for City and Madrid in 2025. There was an ebb and flow to the first half in Manchester, with Erling Haaland crowning a well-worked move for his first goal against Los Blancos.Mbappe's sliced volley with an hour played had a touch of fortune about it but Madrid deserved to be level on the balance of play. Indeed, Haaland's penalty came against the run, only for City to collapse and gift late goals to Brahim Diaz and Jude Bellingham.Guardiola's men were overmatched in the return as Mbappe netted a brilliant hat-trick, with Nico Gonzalez's stoppage-time goal coming as scant consolation in a 6-3 aggregate defeat.Real Madrid vs. Man City (2026 Round of 16)Madrid's 2-1 defeat in the 2025/26 league phase, when City came from behind to win at the Santiago Bernabeu, was one of the results that contributed to Xabi Alonso's mid-season departure. But under new boss Alvaro Arbeloa, Madrid made light of their pre-match status of underdogs when they swept to a 3-0 first leg win on home turf. In the absence of Bellingham and Mbappe, Valverde stepped up with a stunning first-half hat-trick as Guardiola's gamble on an expansive attacking line-up backfired.Vinicius had a tame penalty saved by Gianluigi Buffon at the Bernabeu but prevailed from the spot in Manchester after Bernardo Silva was sent off for handling the blocking the Brazil star's shot on the goalline with his elbow. City acquitted themselves manfully with 10 men and Haaland levelled the score on the night at halftime. Chances came and went after the break, while Jeremy Doku and Rayan Ait-Nouri each had goals chalked off for offside for the hosts, before Vinicius netted his second in stoppage time.
